addresses.name: CAIUnit_SplitGarrisonAndLine
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CAIUnit_SplitGarrisonAndLine(CAIUnit* agent, CList* positions, void* garrisonDivisions, CList* garrisonTargets, int* garrisonCount, int* lineCount)
addresses.comment: 0x4C7AB0 to the `ret 0x18` at 0x4C8EA5, read whole. (1) **Garrison divisions**: over +0x13C, a division with a brigade of type garrison_brigade (CSubUnitDataBase +0x50) gets CUnit +0x2C9 (ai_garrison) = 1 and goes into the output vector; one without, already flagged, stays only while it stands in land we control and is not a role-8 army with air transports about (+0x10C), else its flag is cleared. (2) **Garrison targets**: the hold list +0x17C (slot 80's, best first) - a record of score >= 20.0 in land we control goes onto `garrisonTargets` by descending score, unless it is an ops-area province of under 10 victory points that is not its own depot; for the human's delegated AI (runs_units clear) a province holding a friendly land unit of another agent is skipped; strong = records of score >= 50.0. (3) **The counts**, n = |+0x13C|, posCap = 10 x |positions|: no positions -> garrison = n; no hold provinces (+0x184 == 0) -> line = n - |garrison-brigade divisions|; else front = |+0xC0|, enemies = non-friend land units on front provinces whose controller IsFrontWorthyEnemy, areaSum = the sum of those provinces' areas' sizes; at war on the frontier (+0x364) front x2, front = max(front, areaSum < 7 ? 2 x enemies : enemies), strong = 1 when front <= enemies/3 and strong > 1, enemies x2; lineWant = min(max(enemies, front), posCap); garrison = min(min(+0x184, n), n - lineWant), raised to min(max(targets, |garrison-brigade divisions|) capped at n, n - front) when below that, then to strong; line = n - garrison, the excess over posCap handed back to the garrison. In a scenario game (gamestate +0xD0C) nine tenths of the garrison go to the line. (4) The targets are topped up from the rest of the hold list (any score, best first) until there are `garrison` of them. (5) Per region group (COwnerArea +0x6C) of the first `garrison` targets - the shortfall added to the theatre's largest area's group - the garrison divisions standing or heading there are cut to the group's count (dropping first the one without militia (+1000) or police (+500) whose hold score is lowest; garrison-brigade divisions never) and raised to it from divisions of +0x13C not flagged, standing or heading in the group, facing no country we prepare war on, and at war carrying no armour, light armour, heavy armour or mechanized brigade, nor paratroopers while air transports exist - the best by (10 x its garrison rating (slot 88, RateUnitAsGarrison) + (mean distance to the ops area + 10)/5) x 0.75 on a front province x (1.5 - its organisation share); each pick gets +0x2C9 = 1. The name is ours. See FINDINGS-moving.md, section A.3. On the listing, 2026-11-10: the area sum adds the area's size once for **every** front-worthy front province, whether or not its area has been seen and whether or not it holds a unit - the list of areas it builds is never read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 14.

struct_fields.name: ai_front_relevant
struct_fields.comment:
The byte `CAIUnit::ScoreOpsAreaProvinces` tests to add **+100** to an ops-area province's priority, once per region of that province whose byte is set (0x4BD78F region of the body). **The name is a guess from that single reader and is marked `inferred` accordingly** - what sets it is not established. Read live 2026-10-02 as **0 on all 400+ regions** at the scenario start with the game paused at tick 0, so the +100 never fires there; whether that is because the AI has not started (no CAIUnit has a unit pointer at tick 0) or because the byte is set by war is the open question, and running the game on would answer it.

**It does get set - live 2026-10-02, GER 1942-05-11 war save.** Read 1 on **30 of 2,000+** live regions in a May 1942 war save, against **0 of 400** at the scenario start. So ScoreOpsAreaProvinces's +100-per-region really does fire, and the byte is something a war turns on. That is support for the `inferred` name rather than proof of it: what *sets* it is still unread. (Note the region count: an earlier reading of '400 regions' was the scan limit, not the population.) **It is the word `ai_prio` in the region's block of map/region.txt (inferred from what it holds, the writer not found).** On a game loaded from July 1941 the byte reads 1 on finland_keski_kannas and finland_laatokan_karjala, both marked `ai_prio` in the file, and 0 on the other regions read, none marked; and the seven provinces the Soviet Moskva agent scores 100 higher (by the scale) all lie in marked regions. That the earlier read found it 0 everywhere at the start is unexplained. No `mov byte [reg+0x6D]` writes it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 14.
struct_fields.evidence: Seven provinces read in the running game against the file; the score difference is exactly 100 x the province's scale on each.

struct_fields.name: committed_divisions_copy_first
struct_fields.comment: A second copy of the committed divisions (end +0x140), pushed beside +0x12C; the recall and detach loops change only +0x12C. **It holds every division committed before the reserve is taken out and is not touched afterwards**: on the Soviet Smolensk agent in the running game (2026-11-10) +0x13C held 133, of which 110 are in +0x12C and 23 in +0x15C. So the split of garrison and line, the allied-soil budget and the garrison divisions count the reserve too, and the line can be given more divisions than +0x12C holds. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-liveread.md, section 14.
struct_fields.evidence: The three vectors read and intersected in the running game.
struct_fields.revises: what it holds after the reserve
